title: Excess Dissolved Inorganic Carbon (eDIC) as a Simplifying Metric for Riverine Carbonate Chemistry
content:
Abstract
We develop a new simplifying metric, “excess DIC” (eDIC), dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) minus alkalinity (Alk), to gain insight into the drivers of spatial and temporal variability in riverine pCO2, [H+], and CaCO3 saturation state. [eDIC] is insensitive to most open‐system weathering reactions and well‐approximated by [CO2]–[CO32–] in a wide variety of environments and by [CO2] in a more restricted but still common set of environments (low to moderate pH). eDIC is used to analyze historical carbonate chemistry data of rivers draining the Chesapeake Bay Watershed. Annual‐mean pCO2 and [H+] vary by factors of 3.9 and 27, respectively, across the rivers, but are well‐explained by [eDIC], as are the mean annual cycles of these variables after including effects of temperature on equilibrium constants. Even larger spatial and seasonal variability in CaCO3 saturation state is found, mainly driven by alkalinity, with smaller contributions from eDIC and temperature. [eDIC] generally increases with increasing streamflow, is lower in the summer, and has annual means that increase with the fraction of streamflow from overland flow and decrease with the amount of carbonate rock and soil in the watershed. These patterns are consistent with [eDIC] decreasing with depth in the soil column as a result of a transition from open‐system to closed‐system weathering. [Alk]–[DIC] has seen increasing use in oceanography and we demonstrate here that its negative—excess DIC—shows promise for understanding rivers, particularly when compared to the more‐frequently used [DIC]/[Alk] ratio.

title: Lake hydrochemistry and aquatic plant diversity across permafrost landscapes of Yakutia, Eastern Siberia
content:
Lake hydrochemistry and aquatic plant diversity across permafrost landscapes of Yakutia, Eastern Siberia
Izabella Baisheva, Birgit Heim, Jorge García Molinos, Amelie Stieg, Hanno Meyer, Ramesh Glückler, Kathleen R. Stoof-Leichsenring, Antje Eulenburg, Pier Paul Overduin, Evgenii S. Zakharov, Aital V. Egorov, Paraskovya V. Davydova, Lena A. Ushnitskaya, Sardana N. Levina, Ruslan M. Gorodnichev, Robert Jackisch, Antonie Haas, Nikolai V. Torgovkin, Stefan Kruse, Luidmila A. Pestryakova, and Ulrike Herzschuh
Biogeosciences, 23, 8361–8406, https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-23-8361-2026, 2026
Our study provides a new comprehensive assessment of the limnological state of 66 lakes in the Central Yakutian alaas landscapes and the Verkhoyansk mountain range. Our analyses suggest that specific lake-type properties within the thermokarst lake sequence seem to drive inorganic, organic, and isotopic lake hydrochemistry. Future warming may prolong evaporation exposure, but it may also increase hydrological connectivity, potentially providing more freshwater to the region.

title: Disentangling the biotic and abiotic drivers of evapotranspiration in a degraded raised bog
content:
Disentangling the biotic and abiotic drivers of evapotranspiration in a degraded raised bog
Vincent E. Flemming, Nicolas Behrens, and Mana Gharun
Biogeosciences, 23, 8407–8420, https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-23-8407-2026, 2026
In the context of a changing climate, we examined how vegetation productivity and weather conditions effect cooling in peatland ecosystems. While radiation and vegetation productivity have the greatest influence on cooling during the growing season, water table depth and air dryness are the foremost factors outside growing season. A drought threshold limits evapotranspiration via canopy water regulation. Our results are crucial for understanding future heat and climate regulation of peatlands.

title: Contrasting Drivers of Summer Tropical Cyclone Genesis Potential Between the East China Sea and the Tropical Western North Pacific
content:
Abstract
Tropical cyclone (TC) genesis over the western North Pacific (WNP) is strongly influenced by large‐scale dynamical conditions, yet the mechanisms responsible for regional variations during boreal summer remain unclear. Using the dynamic genesis potential index (DGPI), we investigate regional contrasts in summer TC genesis potential across the WNP and the mechanisms governing its interannual variability and long‐term trends. The results reveal opposing long‐term DGPI trends, with a significant increase over the East China Sea (ECS) and a significant decrease over the tropical western North Pacific (TWNP), indicating a redistribution of dynamical genesis potential rather than a basinwide coherent change. Over the ECS, both interannual variability and the long‐term increase in DGPI are associated with a strengthened meridional sea surface temperature (SST) gradient over the North Pacific, which induces anomalous low‐level easterlies and positive relative vorticity anomalies that favor TC genesis. Over the TWNP, interannual DGPI variability is modulated by air–sea interactions associated with the spring‐to‐summer North Pacific Meridional Mode, whereas the long‐term decline is primarily linked to an intensified zonal SST gradient over the equatorial Pacific. The resulting equatorial easterly anomalies contribute to decreasing relative vorticity over the key region, reducing dynamical favorability for TC genesis. These relationships are further supported by Liang–Kleeman information flow analysis. Our results demonstrate a regionally asymmetric response of summer TC genesis potential over the WNP to large‐scale SST forcing and suggest that projections based on basin‐averaged indices may obscure opposing subregional changes, particularly in marginal seas such as the ECS.

title: Dynamical Mechanism of Rossby Waves Triggering Equilibrium State Transitions Within the Mindanao‐New Guinea Confluence
content:
Abstract
Transitions between the penetrating and choking states of the Mindanao–New Guinea Confluence (MNGC) influence regional circulation and the Indonesian Throughflow (ITF), yet the dynamical pathway linking remote Pacific Rossby waves to these transitions remains unclear. We investigate this pathway using a high‐resolution regional ocean model with idealized equatorial and off‐equatorial Rossby wave signals imposed at its eastern boundary, with wave parameters constrained by satellite observations. The experiments show that equatorial Rossby waves with different phases shift the timing of seasonal state transitions, whereas waves imposed farther off the equator exert weaker effects under the tested configurations. The key mechanism is a meridional seesaw in sea surface height and thermocline depth anomalies between the Mindanao and Halmahera Eddies. Rossby waves modify this seesaw structure, alter the meridional pressure gradients and the retroflection position of the Mindanao Current, and thereby modulate transitions between the penetrating and choking states. The associated zonal geostrophic transport anomalies redistribute the Mindanao Current between westward leakage into the Sulawesi Sea and eastward retroflection into the Pacific, regulating ITF transport through Makassar Strait in the upper 300 m. Particularly, the experiments showed that the Pacific equatorial Rossby waves could weaken the ITF by altering the equilibrium state transitions in 2016, indicating that the meridional seesaw mechanism may be applicable to the multi‐timescale variations. This study has proposed a novel mechanism for the equilibrium state transitions within the MNGC and has provided new insights into the ITF variations.

title: Modes of Ross Gyre Variability: Strengthening and Expansion
content:
Abstract
The circulation of the Ross Gyre has been shown to influence ocean temperatures over the West Antarctic continental shelf through expansions of its eastern boundary. While the gyre is bounded by Antarctica and bathymetric ridges to the south, west and north, it lacks topographic constraints to the east. Thus, the processes controlling shifts in the eastern boundary remain unclear, with previous studies assuming a direct link between gyre strength and eastward extent. Here we use a 60‐year ocean–sea ice model simulation and additional perturbation experiments to investigate sources of Ross Gyre variability. We find that variations in the eastern boundary are not always concurrent with variations in gyre strength and identify two modes of circulation: a strengthening‐only mode driven by stronger westerly winds, and a strengthening‐with‐expansion mode associated with changes in the Amundsen Sea Low. We further show that these differing responses of the gyre depend on the vertical structure of the circulation. While west of the Marie Byrd plateau the gyre spans the entire water column, toward the Antarctic peninsula its circulation is confined to deeper layers, extending beneath the Antarctic Circumpolar Current. A strengthening of the Amundsen Sea Low drives sea level changes involving a rapid barotropic adjustment that weakens the Antarctic Circumpolar Current, permitting a stronger eastward extension of the Ross Gyre. Moreover, the strengthened extension occupies a larger fraction of the water column impinging onto the warm Circumpolar Deep Water layer, with implications for heat transport in the region.

title: Climate‐Associated Adaptive Divergence of MHC Class I Gene in an Ungulate Species, Gazella subgutturosa, From an Extreme Inland‐Island Habitat
content:
ABSTRACT
Island biogeography theory provides a classical framework for understanding how habitat isolation drives biological evolution, yet the ecological mechanisms by which ‘inland islands’ shape adaptive evolution of functional immune genes remain unclear. Here we investigated the diversity, selection, and local adaptation of MHC class I exons 2 and 3 in goitered gazelle (Gazella subgutturosa) populations from the Tarim basin (an ‘inland island’) and northern Xinjiang, China. We generated amplicon sequences for 158 individuals and identified 100 and 47 unique variants for exons 2 and 3, respectively. Exon 2 showed higher diversity and stronger positive selection than exon 3, while exon 3 carried in‐frame deletions and a recombination event exclusive to the Tarim basin population. Private variants from the two regions exhibited opposite correlations with temperature and precipitation. Redundancy analysis revealed that exon 2 is primarily associated with temperature gradients, whereas exon 3 is correlated with both temperature and precipitation. Neutral microsatellite markers revealed strong geographic isolation without recent genetic bottlenecks between the two regions, while MHC‐I genes showed neither isolation‐by‐distance nor isolation‐by‐environment, but were significantly associated with temperature and precipitation related climatic variables. Multiple lines of evidence—private positively selected sites, a private supertype, and independent phylogenetic clustering—suggest that exon 3 has undergone adaptive differentiation in the isolated arid habitat. Altogether, these patterns are consistent with the possibility that inland‐island isolation, through climatic heterogeneity, may contribute to local adaptation of MHC‐I, providing the first insights into adaptive evolution of immune genes in an inland‐island system and offering new perspectives for conservation of isolated ungulate populations.

摘要
摘要岛屿生物地理学理论为理解栖息地隔离如何驱动生物演化提供经典框架，但“内陆岛屿”塑造功能性免疫基因适应性演化的生态机制仍不清楚。本研究探讨中国塔里木盆地(“内陆岛屿”)与北疆地区鹅喉羚(Gazella subgutturosa)种群MHC I类基因第2和第3外显子的多样性、自然选择及局域适应。我们获得158份样本的扩增子序列，并分别在第2和第3外显子中鉴定出100个和47个独特变异序列。第2外显子较第3外显子表现出更高的多样性和更强的正选择信号，而第3外显子携带仅见于塔里木盆地种群的框内缺失和一个重组事件。两个地区的特有变异序列与温度和降水相关气候因子呈相反的相关关系。冗余分析表明，第2外显子主要与温度梯度相关，而第3外显子与温度和降水均相关。微卫星标记显示，两个地区之间存在强烈的地理隔离，但近期未发生遗传瓶颈；而MHC基因既未表现出距离隔离，也未表现出环境隔离，但与温度和降水相关的气候变量显著相关。多方面的证据——包括特有正选择位点、特有超型以及独立的系统发育聚类——表明第3外显子在隔离的干旱生境中经历独特的适应性分化。总体而言，这些模式与以下假设一致:内陆岛屿隔离可通过气候异质性促进MHC I类的局域适应。该研究为内陆岛屿系统中免疫基因的适应性演化提供首次见解，并为隔离的有蹄类种群保护提供了新视角。

title: Disturbance shifts belowground plant nutrient acquisition strategies in a tropical peat swamp forest
content:
Abstract
Tropical peatlands store 25% of the tropical terrestrial carbon (C) pool. Despite global significance, tropical peat swamps have been extensively degraded through drainage and land use change. Yet, the biological processes belowground that underlie C cycling in these ecosystems remain poorly understood. Roots, often in association with mycorrhizal fungi, play a pivotal role in biomass production, turnover, and nutrient acquisition. Changes in belowground traits in response to degradation could therefore have cascading effects on C cycling. Here, we examined fine and coarse root biomass, fine root traits, and ectomycorrhizal colonization along a disturbance gradient from an intact peat swamp forest to a drained, vegetative peatland in a Southeast Asian peat swamp forest. We hypothesized that increasing disturbance would shift plant C allocation from ectomycorrhizal fungi to fine root biomass. We found that as disturbance increased, fine root biomass increased by 37%, suggesting greater aeration and increased investment. Roots became thicker with a lower exploration capacity as depth increased. Ectomycorrhizal colonization decreased by 28% from intact to disturbed peat forest stands, indicating that disturbance reduced fungal associations. Collectively, we demonstrate that disturbance shifts belowground plant nutrient acquisition strategies, disrupting key plant‐fungal mutualisms, and potentially alters belowground processes in tropical peat swamp forests.

title: Erratum to “Environmental and demographic mechanisms underlying population dynamics provide relative stability in an island songbird”
Erratum to “PROCEED v6.1: Phenotypic rates of change evolutionary and ecological database”
Groundfish With Diverse Life Histories Increase in Size and Abundance With Proximity to Spatial Protections
content:
Groundfish abundance (CPUE) and body size increased with proximity to Rockfish Conservation Areas (RCAs) across the Central Coast of British Columbia, Canada (map, left). Both responses strengthened as RCAs aged, and abundance responses varied with species life history (rmax) and pre‐RCA harvest (right panels; thick and thin bars show 66% and 95% confidence intervals).

ABSTRACT
Detecting positive responses to marine spatial protections, both in situ and as spillover effects, is critical for fisheries management yet difficult in practice. We leveraged 18 years of data on 28 groundfish species, collected by four Indigenous Nations in Pacific Canada, to assess ecological responses inside and up to 160 km outside spatially protected Rockfish Conservation Areas (RCAs). Body sizes and abundances were greatest inside RCAs and increased with proximity to RCAs. Abundance responses emerged faster (at younger RCA ages) for species with high rmax, as predicted, but body size responses emerged faster for species with low rmax, counter to predictions. Our study illustrates a general framework for jointly inferring in situ recovery and spillover benefits using a novel hierarchical geostatistical model that integrated long time series; observations made inside, near, and far from seven RCAs; and multiple species and survey methods spanning a 500‐m depth range.

title: Historical and potential future importance of marine megafauna subsidies to terrestrial ecosystems
content: Marine megafauna exert tremendous influence on the structure and function of ocean ecosystems, yet mounting evidence shows that their ecological impacts also cross the land–sea interface and modify terrestrial ecosystem dynamics. Marine megafauna—especially marine mammals and sea turtles—connect land and sea by serving as large, calorically rich food sources for terrestrial consumers and by transferring marine‐derived nutrients onto land as carrion, eggs, placentas, and excreta. We synthesize empirical studies from around the world to characterize the broad suite of terrestrial consumers that exploit marine mammals and sea turtles as food and the ecological impacts arising from these cross‐ecosystem resource subsidies. We identified 224 megafauna–consumer species pairs and diverse ecological effects impacting terrestrial consumers, populations, communities, and ecosystems. Given that commercial exploitation has decimated marine megafauna populations globally, land–sea linkages once mediated by these animals have declined from historical periods to the present day, yet megafauna recoveries hold potential to restore these marine–terrestrial connections and reshape coastal ecosystem dynamics.

title: Global monitoring of wildlife mortality through participatory science in near‐real time
content: Detection of wildlife mortality events is critical for timely conservation and natural resource management. We present an open‐source, web‐based, decision‐support tool that queries, aggregates, and summarizes participatory‐science data from iNaturalist to monitor mortality events worldwide. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach using four case studies spanning taxonomic, spatial, and temporal scales. In Canada and the US, high peaks of bird mortality coincided with zoonotic risk during avian influenza outbreaks. Across Africa, we detected 45 mortality events of threatened species in March 2026. In California, recorded mammal mortality was associated with human infrastructure, including proximity to roads, and to a lesser extent, the human footprint. Mortality of pumas (Puma concolor) was detected across 12 countries, highlighting the need for international cooperation to conserve mobile species. Our tool enables resource managers to flag emerging threats and empowers participatory scientists to monitor and integrate mortality records for conservation.

title: TopoPPI: A geometry-aware platform for visualization and low-distortion mapping of protein-protein interaction interfaces
content:
by Shuyu Zhong

Protein–protein interfaces encode molecular recognition through spatially organized contacts, yet their buried, curved surfaces are difficult to inspect as a whole. Flattening these surfaces can expose interface organization but introduces geometric distortion and may divide individual residues into disconnected regions. We present TopoPPI, a geometry-aware platform that converts interaction surfaces into low-distortion two-dimensional atlases while retaining links to source atoms, residues and contacts. TopoPPI extends OptCuts with a contact-weighted penalty for seam-induced fragmentation of residue footprints—the surface regions assigned to individual residues—jointly balancing continuity, seam length and distortion. In a leakage-controlled benchmark of 2,236 experimental complexes, the geometry-only OptCuts foundation achieved 88.39% lower family-weighted scale-fair distortion than the next-best tested parameterization across 2,209 complete comparable outputs. Across 2,204 exact-domain comparisons, TopoPPI reduced family-weighted residue-footprint fragmentation by 12.81% (95% confidence interval, 11.50–14.05%), with a 2.60% increase in normalized seam length and a 0.061% increase in scale-fair distortion. Continuity gains extended to 1,180 fixed-pose pairs of AlphaFold monomer models and 145 predicted complexes, with fragmentation reductions of 18.60% and 11.65%, respectively. Functionally annotated antibody and colicin–immunity interfaces demonstrated reconnection of the footprints of experimentally characterized binding and specificity residues. Further applications mapped published binding and folding free-energy estimates onto the KRAS–RAF1 interface and compared shared receptor residues across two growth-hormone recognition sites. Available through graphical and command-line interfaces, TopoPPI provides a residue-aware visualization framework for integrating structural contacts and functional annotations within geometrically controlled interface maps.

title: GapCNV: A comprehensive framework for CNV detection in low-input DNA sequencing data
content:
by Xuanxuan Yu, Fei Qin, Shiwei Liu, Noah J. Brown, Xiao Fan, Qing Lu, Guoshuai Cai, Jennifer L. Guler, Feifei Xiao

Copy number variants (CNVs) are prevalent in both diploid and haploid genomes and contribute to genome evolution and phenotypic diversity. However, CNV detection in low-input data, including low-cell and single-cell sequencing data, remains challenging due to the shallow and highly uneven read counts and amplification bias. Another challenge lies in selecting reference samples, which are used to provide a baseline for defining copy-number losses or gains. Normalization using references containing common CNVs can lead to cancellation of true CNV signals or false CNV calls. Here, we develop GapCNV, a statistical framework for CNV detection in low-input DNA sequencing data from both haploid and diploid genomes. GapCNV uses preliminary cell clustering and shared CNV profiles to construct bin-specific pseudo-references from cells inferred to have the copy-neutral state. This strategy reduces the incorporation of common CNVs into the normalization baseline and thereby preserves common CNV signals. We evaluated GapCNV using simulations with and without amplification biases and datasets from Plasmodium falciparum, human breast cancer and melanoma. In simulations, GapCNV achieved high precision rate while maintaining competitive sensitivity, with advantages for detecting short and common CNVs. In P. falciparum, GapCNV detected the known CNVs and recovered the short CNV more frequently than the benchmarking methods. In the melanoma cell line and human breast tumors, GapCNV recovered bulk or single-cell derived copy number profile across individual cells. These results show that adaptive, bin-specific pseudo-reference construction can improve CNV detection when reliable normal controls are unavailable.

title: Hierarchical data-driven dynamical surrogate models of social decision-making
content:
by Manuel Brenner, Ismail Guennouni, Daniel Durstewitz, Stephanie N. L. Schmidt, Stefanie Lis, Peter Kirsch, Georgia Koppe

Social decision making is inherently complex, shaped by dynamic trust building, biases, and adaptive strategies. Yet in laboratory settings, its study is often constrained by small datasets that nonetheless encode rich and sophisticated cognitive processes. This scarcity has historically limited modeling approaches to hand-tailored frameworks that embed strong priors about the underlying mechanisms. Recent advances in data-driven modeling of latent dynamical processes provide an alternative, extracting generative models directly from behavioral data without restrictive assumptions. Building on these methods, we derive hierarchical digital surrogates from sparse, non-Gaussian investment sequences in repeated trust games. Our approach proceeds in three stages. First, we demonstrate that, despite the limited data, the inferred models can accurately predict future investments and outperform theory-driven reinforcement-learning and Bayesian cognitive models, establishing predictive validity and providing a solid baseline for subsequent mechanistic analyses. Second, we analyze the latent dynamics of these models and show that they capture mechanistic structure in how investments and choice uncertainty are organized in state space and how social versus non-social cues are represented, in a way that parallels patterns observed directly in the empirical behavior. Third, we exploit the generative nature of the hierarchical digital surrogates to run in-silico experiments beyond the original data, such as probing how specific cues steer participants into trusting or mistrusting states and simulating responses to novel, unobserved cue-outcome combinations and trustee strategies. Together, this work demonstrates how generative digital surrogates open a new path toward mechanistic, data-driven accounts of social interaction dynamics that both reproduce observed behavior and support hypothesis generation in virtual environments.

title: A beam–membrane biomechanical vocal fold model incorporating posturing and glottal conformation
content:
by Mohamed A. Serry, Matías Zañartu, Sean D. Peterson

The posture of the vocal folds produced by laryngeal muscle activation plays a central role in determining the dynamics of voice production. Abnormal vocal fold configurations are frequently associated with inefficient phonation and a variety of voice disorders. Although diverse glottal closure patterns have been observed clinically, the biomechanical mechanisms governing their dynamic behavior and resulting phonatory characteristics remain incompletely understood. Moreover, existing numerical models that incorporate the effects of the intrinsic musculature on posturing and glottal conformation are computationally expensive, which limits their suitability for large-scale parametric investigations. In this work, we introduce a computationally inexpensive vocal fold (VF) model wherein the body and cover VF layers are treated as a composite beam and a coupled membrane, respectively. Intrinsic laryngeal muscle activation, in addition to positioning the arytenoid cartilages and cricothyroid joint, introduces moments at the boundaries of the structure that influence glottal conformation. The model produces phonatory characteristics that are qualitatively consistent with those reported in high-fidelity finite-element models and clinical studies, thereby supporting its predictive capability while offering substantial computational advantage. The proposed framework provides biomechanical insights into the influence of incomplete glottal closure on phonation dynamics and may serve as a computationally tractable tool for investigating mechanisms underlying certain voice disorders.

title: Exploring the potential of bile fluid dynamics analysis to inform clinical strategies for choledochal cysts: Experimental and numerical studies
content:
by Yidan Shang, Jiaying Liu, Wentao Sun, Renquan Tu, Xueren Li, Xiaojian Ni, Houbao Liu, Jiyuan Tu

Surgical intervention is essential for choledochal cysts (CCs) due to their high lifetime risk of progressing to cholangiocarcinoma, yet management strategies vary worldwide. Given bile fluid’s vital role in digestion, investigating bile flow dynamics may provide surgeons with additional insights for treatment planning. In this study, one MRI-based healthy adult scan was used to reconstruct biliary system, which was then modified according to Todani classifications to generate eight CC types. Particle Image Velocimetry was used to first visualize local velocity field, followed by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of bile emptying to analyze pathological non-Newtonian bile flow. Wall shear stress (WSS), a key biomechanical parameter, was visualized through 2D surface mapping for comparative evaluation. Results showed consistently low velocity in dilated regions, suggesting bile accumulation in CCs, particularly in Types 1a, 2, 4a, and 4b. While WSS changes were minimal in the healthy biliary system, extreme gradients, up to 10,000-fold emerged in CCs, especially Types 1a, 2, and 4a. These findings highlight that bile flow characteristics are primarily dictated by localized anatomical abnormalities, aligning with surgical interventions that target dilated regions. These findings demonstrate the potential of CFD to provide additional biomechanical insights into bile flow abnormalities associated with different CC types, which may serve as a reference for future clinical investigations.

title: Ontology pre-training improves machine learning-based predictions for metabolites
content:
by Charlotte Tumescheit, Martin Glauer, Simon Flügel, Martin Larralde, Fabian Neuhaus, Till Mossakowski, Janna Hastings

Deep learning has recently led to multiple breakthroughs in longstanding biological problems. Recent advances have shown that integration of expert knowledge can improve deep learning model predictive performance in complex domains such as biology. Bio-ontologies offer a rich source of curated biological knowledge that can be harnessed to this end. Here, we describe an intuitive and generalisable approach to embed the knowledge contained in a classification hierarchy derived from a bio-ontology into a deep learning model as an intermediate training step between general-purpose pre-training and task-specific fine-tuning: a process that we call’ontology pre-training’. We show that this approach leads to an improvement in predictive performance and a reduction in training time for a broad range of prediction tasks related to metabolite functions, activities and properties in living systems, using a range of datasets derived from MoleculeNet. We see the biggest improvement for regression tasks, e.g., prediction of lipophilicity and aqueous solubility of molecules, and a robust improvement for most classification tasks. Our approach can be adapted for a wide range of knowledge sources, models and prediction tasks.

title: Exploring the mechanism of oxfendazole in inhibiting osteosarcoma-induced osteolysis based on single-cell RNA seqsuencing
content:
by Jifeng Miao, Pintian Wang, Wenyu Feng, Haiyi Quan, Yunhua Lin, Gejin Wei, Fake Meng, Shanhang Li, Mingxiu Yang, Binyuan Ning, Jingxin Deng, Liang Xiong, Jianming Hu, Yun Liu, Qingjun Wei

Osteosarcoma-associated osteolysis represents a major obstacle in the management of osteosarcoma. Within the osteolytic microenvironment, interactions between osteoclasts and tumor cells facilitate tumor proliferation and metastatic dissemination, and contribute to the development of pathological fractures. However, conventional osteoclast-targeting agents are insufficient to effectively suppress osteosarcoma-driven bone resorption. In this study, single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to identify critical regulators involved in osteoclast differentiation in the context of osteosarcoma. Using the Beyondcell platform, drugs targeting osteoclast-related signaling pathways were screened, and oxfendazole (OFN) was identified as a potential therapeutic candidate, with ANXA2 recognized as a key associated target. In vitro osteoclastogenesis assays and an in vivo tibial orthotopic osteosarcoma model demonstrated that oral administration of OFN via gavage effectively suppressed osteoclast formation and osteolytic activity, as confirmed by micro-CT and histopathological analyses. But OFN alone did not significantly inhibit osteosarcoma growth but effectively reduced osteoclast-mediated osteolysis. In addition, qRT-PCR and immunohistochemistry confirmed that OFN downregulates ANXA2 expression in vitro and in vivo, thereby impairing osteoclast differentiation. Molecular dynamics simulations combined with in-vitro validation further suggested that OFN may interact with the transcription factor ZNF530, leading to reduced ANXA2 transcription. In conclusion, the integration of single-cell RNA sequencing with the Beyondcell algorithm enabled the identification of OFN as a potent candidate agent for osteosarcoma-induced osteolysis. OFN attenuates osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption by suppressing ANXA2 expression. These findings provide preclinical evidence supporting the therapeutic potential of OFN in the treatment of osteosarcoma-associated osteolysis.

title: Dynamic functional connectivity reveals evolving neural activity states of alcohol-seeking in rats
content:
by Yujing Zhang, Nicholas M. Timme, Mintao Liu, Christopher C. Lapish, Joaquín Goñi

The brain mechanisms underlying persistent alcohol-seeking in Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) remain incompletely understood. To investigate this behavior, we characterized the temporal evolution of neural activity states in the anterior cingulate cortex of freely behaving rats performing an aversion-resistant drinking (ARD) task. Alcohol-preferring (P) rats were assessed, as they reliably exhibit ARD when alcohol is devalued with the bitter tastant quinine. P rats were compared with Wistar rats, which progress slower to ARD, as indicated by cessation of drinking following quinine devaluation. Using dynamic functional connectivity analyses of spike-train recordings, we identified latent neural states corresponding to seeking and non-seeking phases. We then integrated the latent-state decoding of neural activity with a seeking intensity model derived from the observed drinking behavior. This framework revealed that the decoded latent neural states closely tracked behavior. Furthermore, during alcohol-reinforced sessions, neural and behavioral measures of drinking or non-drinking states were strongly aligned in both strains. However, after alcohol devaluation, this alignment diverged in P rats but remained consistent in Wistars. The inability of P rats to acquire stable neural states following devaluation suggests impaired formation of latent states as a neural mechanism of ARD, offering insights into the cognitive vulnerabilities that may sustain AUD.

title: Fragmented decision-making hinders the transition to sustainable sand alternatives
content:
Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43017-026-00858-z

Sand extraction sustains development but destabilizes ecosystems. Transitioning to sustainable alternatives will require decision-making that reconciles sand’s economic, social and environmental values.

title: WNK-SPAK/OSR1 signaling pathway facilitates ictal activity via reduced neuronal chloride extrusion rate
content: Seizures upregulate Na<sup>+</sup>-K<sup>+</sup>–2Cl<sup>−</sup> (NKCC1)-mediated Cl<sup>−</sup> influx and downregulate K<sup>+</sup>-Cl<sup>−</sup> (KCC2)-mediated Cl<sup>−</sup> efflux via the WNK-SPAK/OSR1 kinases, leading to cytoplasmic chloride ([Cl<sup>−</sup>]<sub>i</sub>) accumulation, reduced GABAergic inhibition, and anticonvulsant failure. Early studies found that inhibiting WNK-kinase reduced baseline [Cl<sup>−</sup>]<sub>i</sub> (E<sub>Cl</sub>) and seizures via increased KCC2 activity. However, increased KCC2 activity alone should not affect E<sub>Cl</sub>, whose determinants are more complex. We determined the net effects of the WNK-SPAK/OSR1 pathway inhibitor WNK463 on E<sub>Cl</sub> and [Cl<sup>−</sup>]<sub>i</sub> transients during spontaneous ictal-like discharges (ILDs) in organotypic hippocampal slice cultures from mice. We found that WNK463 reduced interictal [Cl<sup>−</sup>]<sub>i</sub>, but did not change baseline [Cl<sup>−</sup>]<sub>i</sub> measured in the presence of TTX. WNK463 enhanced neuronal Cl<sup>−</sup> extrusion during and after ILDs before abolishing ILDs. Pharmacological inhibition and targeted siRNA silencing demonstrated that the anti-ictal effects of WNK463 involved both NKCC1 and KCC2. Our data support a mechanism whereby mutual NKCC1 inhibition and KCC2 activation via the WNK-SPAK/OSR1 pathway exert powerful anti-ictal effects by facilitating [Cl<sup>−</sup>]<sub>i</sub> extrusion during ILDs.

title: Hierarchical neural circuit theory of normalization and inter-areal communication
content: The primate brain exhibits a hierarchical, modular architecture with conserved microcircuits executing canonical computations across reciprocally connected cortical areas. We present a hierarchical neural circuit theory with feedback connections that dynamically implements divisive normalization across its hierarchy. In a two-stage instantiation (V1 ↔ V2), increasing feedback from V2 to V1 amplifies responses in both areas. We analytically derive power spectra (V1) and coherence spectra (V1-V2) as functions of frequency (f) and compare them with experimental observations: peaks in both spectra shift to higher frequencies with increased stimulus contrast, and power decays as 1/f4 at high frequencies. The closed-form spectra are validated against direct stochastic simulation of the full nonlinear circuit across contrasts. The theory further predicts distinctive spectral signatures of feedback and input gain modulation. Crucially, the theory offers a unified view of inter-areal communication, defined as the ability to linearly predict neural activity in one brain area from neural activity in another, with emergent features consistent with empirical observations of both communication subspaces and inter-areal coherence. It admits a low-dimensional communication subspace, where inter-areal communication is lower-dimensional than within-area communication. It further predicts that: (1) increasing feedback strength enhances inter-areal communication and diminishes within-area communication, without altering the subspace dimensionality; (2) communication is strongest, and the subspace dimensionality lowest, at the frequencies at which V1-V2 coherence peaks; (3) normalization reduces the subspace dimensionality. Finally, a three-area (V1 ↔ V4 and V1 ↔ V5) instantiation of the theory demonstrates that differential feedback from higher to lower cortical areas dictates their dynamic functional connectivity. Altogether, our theory provides a robust and analytically tractable framework for generating experimentally testable predictions about normalization, inter-areal communication, and functional connectivity.

title: Transposons contribute to splice-isoform diversity in the Drosophila brain
content: The extraordinary complexity of the brain depends in part on the vast diversity of mRNA isoforms it expresses, often in a cell-type specific manner. In a recent study, we found that intronic transposable elements (TEs) are spliced into neural transcripts and diversify the splice isoform repertoire of neurons and glia (Treiber and Waddell, 2020). A recent paper by Azad et al. revisits these findings using their TIDAL analysis pipeline applied to our published data (Azad et al., 2024). Their analysis did not find any of the splicing reads we reported and although they used RT-PCR to test seven of the 264 TE–gene pairs we had previously reported, they failed to validate TE–gene splicing in any of them. Here, we conduct a quantitative analysis of TE exonisation and show that intronic TE insertions are frequently recruited as alternative exons, with exon usage ranging from rare events to near-complete inclusion in transcripts. We implement this analysis in an improved version of our TEChim software and present clear support for TE–gene splicing at the seven loci tested by Azad et al. We also identify methodological issues in the experimental and computational design of the Azad et al. study that likely explains their failure to detect TE–gene chimeras, while demonstrating that TE–gene splicing can be detected by RT-PCR under appropriate experimental conditions. Together, our data demonstrates that TE splice isoforms are not rare artefacts but measurable and biologically relevant features of the Drosophila brain transcriptome that may contribute to the molecular complexity and functional adaptability of the brain.

title: New Early Cretaceous Paleomagnetic Results From the Jiuxi Basin: Tectonic Implications for the Sinistral Strike‐slip of the Altyn Tagh Fault
content:
Abstract
Constraining the timing and early kinematic evolution of the Altyn Tagh Fault (ATF) is critical for understanding pre‐Cenozoic intracontinental deformation in northern Tibet. We present new paleomagnetic data from Lower Cretaceous in the Jiuxi Basin, northeastern Tibetan Plateau. Together with published paleomagnetic results, our results identify two phases of vertical‐axis rotation in the northeastern Tibetan Plateau: a general clockwise rotation of ∼30°–50° relative to Eurasia prior to 106.6 Ma in the North Qilian Shan induced by regional E‐W extension and dextral boundary faulting, followed by a 10–20° counterclockwise rotation relative to Eurasia between 106.6 and 80 Ma or 13.5–9 Ma caused by sinistral strike‐slip of ATF. Our study provides new Early Cretaceous paleomagnetic data from northeastern Tibetan Plateau, constrains the Early Cretaceous tectonic evolution of the region, and further proposes an early transtensional deformation model along the North Qilian Shan and a later distributed strike‐slip deformation model along the ATF.

title: Abrupt Shifts in Subpolar Gyre Deep Convection Under Pre‐Industrial Climate Conditions
content:
Abstract
Recent observations indicate two distinct drivers of interrupted winter convection in the Labrador Sea: anomalous atmospheric forcing and the advection of freshwater anomalies. Here we test whether these mechanisms arise spontaneously under stationary pre‐industrial climate conditions using six medium to high‐resolution CMIP6 control simulations. We identify recurrent shutdowns of Subpolar Gyre deep convection driven primarily by persistent negative NAO phases, which suppress winter surface heat loss and inhibit convective preconditioning. In addition, rare but more persistent shutdowns occur when freshwater anomalies of Arctic origin reach the Labrador Sea, enhancing stratification and sea‐ice formation. Our results demonstrate that both observed drivers of Labrador Sea convection interruption are intrinsic features of internal variability of state‐of‐the‐art climate models, providing a baseline for assessing how these drivers respond to anthropogenic warming.

title: A Theory of Meltwater‐ Versus Polynya‐Dominated Ice Shelf Cavities
content:
Abstract
Oceanic melting of Antarctic ice shelves plays a key role in ice sheet mass balance and retreat. Yet efforts to project future changes in melt are hindered by limited understanding of its environmental controls. Here, we introduce a theoretical framework with two components. The first is a novel classification of cavities which distinguishes between ice shelves which are “disconnected” and “connected” to offshore waters based on the buoyancy budget at their front. The second is a pair of scaling theories which predict the basal melt within “disconnected” and “connected” cavities based on the horizontal buoyancy gradients within the cavity. We demonstrate in idealized simulations and observations that this framework predicts whether ice shelf cavities are connected or disconnected and explains >∼90% ${ >} \sim 90\%$ of the variance in their melt. This framework represents a significant advance in our understanding of first‐order cavity dynamics and could aid in the development of new basal melt parameterizations.

title: Anomalous Pressure‐Dependent Viscosity of Basaltic Melts and Its Role in Asthenosphere Melt Accumulation
content:
Abstract
The asthenosphere's mechanical weakness enables plate tectonics, but its origin is debated. Partial melt has been proposed to cause this softening, yet recent studies suggest that the measured viscosity minimum in basaltic melts—an essential control on melt mobility—is an experimental artifact. Using quantum mechanics‐based, machine learning‐accelerated molecular dynamics, we extend simulation timescales by >103 and achieve percent‐level precision. We show that basaltic melt exhibits a robust viscosity minimum (∼20% below 1‐bar values) at ∼3 GPa, driven by pressure‐induced reorganization of aluminum coordination that facilitates shear relaxation while silicon–oxygen polyhedra remain structurally rigid. Our results reveal a depth‐dependent rheological transition: melt mobility peaks below ∼150 km, promoting efficient extraction, but declines sharply during ascent, causing melt to stagnate beneath the lithosphere. This mechanism provides a physical basis for the dual seismic signatures of a melt‐depleted deep asthenosphere and a melt‐enriched layer near the lithosphere–asthenosphere boundary.

title: Weathering Flux Calculations From Climate Model Outputs Show a Decrease in Alkalinity Fluxes to the Ocean During the Last Deglaciation
content:
Abstract
Variations in chemical weathering rates during the last deglaciation remain poorly constrained, although some studies suggest little net change because climatic and sea‐level changes act in opposite directions. Here, we use climate model outputs to calculate weathering fluxes with empirical equations, estimating their impacts on the deglacial evolution of riverine alkalinity fluxes to the ocean. With our model ensemble, we obtain a decreasing trend of alkalinity fluxes, resulting from loess erosion and flooding shelves (whose effects are counteracting those of a climate getting warmer and wetter). Such a reduction in alkalinity source could affect the marine carbon cycle, contributing to the deglacial atmospheric CO2 ${\text{CO}}_{2}$ increase. Our results also underline the need for further model development to reduce runoff biases and implement evolving coastlines in Earth System Models, as well as the importance of a good representation of lithological data.

title: Explaining Convection and Instability Scalings in Radiative‐Convective Equilibrium
content:
Abstract
In Earth's tropics, stronger radiative cooling enhances convection. Numerical experiments reveal that cloud cover increases nearly linearly with the cooling rate, while updraft velocity remains almost constant. However, atmospheric instability decreases under stronger cooling. We develop a simple two‐layer cloud model to explain how these scalings arise. The cloud cover and updraft velocity scalings follow naturally from mass continuity and an assumption for the dissipation rate. The scaling for instability requires a further closure assumption. Allowing the updraft velocity to depend on low‐level cloud cover is an attractive possibility consistent with cloud‐updraft interactions, and predicts an instability dependence consistent with simulations. Larger cloud cover under stronger cooling compensates for the reduction in instability through cloud‐updraft interactions, allowing updraft velocities to remain approximately unchanged despite lower CAPE. The framework reconciles CAPE‐based interpretations of convection with the observed RCE scalings, providing a physically based foundation for prognostic convective parameterizations.

title: The Response of Onset and Withdrawal of the Indian Summer Monsoon to Volcanic Aerosols
content:
Abstract
Large volcanic eruptions are a source of climate variability, affecting the seasonal mean precipitation of the Indian summer monsoon. However, the extent to which changes in seasonal precipitation can be attributed to variations in monsoon length versus monsoon intensity has remained unclear. Using large ensemble simulations of idealized volcanic eruptions at varying latitudes, we find that the monsoon onset and withdrawal change by a few weeks compared to an unforced case. Southern (Northern) hemispheric eruptions extend (shorten) the Indian summer monsoon in the year following the eruption. We show that these changes in the length of the monsoon season are more important in controlling the response of total monsoon rainfall to eruptions than changes to the intensity of rainfall. We explain our results using the low‐level jet and Inter‐tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) frameworks, which have been used to explain the internal variability of the monsoon onset.
